title: Why she stayed
notes: Come up / stay down. She explains why she stayed on the ground for five
months. The player can argue, and should be able to lose the argument.

lines.text: INCOMING -- U.S.S. ADIRONDACK
Shepard. Have you got a minute? A real one.
INCOMING -- U.S.S. ADIRONDACK
I tried you yesterday. I'll assume the dead were busy.
Have you got a minute now?
Something you asked, or didn't. Why I stayed down.
February to July, on the ground, with a ship overhead
begging me to come up. I owe somebody the answer.

options.text: I figured it was the work.

lines.text: I owe the ten who stayed because I did. You'll do.
Because it was the best work anybody in my field
will ever get to do. A living world, unannounced.
And because I could pass. Six months of market days.
The others could sit in orbit and read my notes.
Ten of them didn't. They came down because I did.
That's kind. It's also not how command works.
A lieutenant who plants a flag is a place to stand.
I knew that. I planted it anyway.

options.text: Then you'd better start carrying it.

lines.text: Some of them. Yes. Say it again if it helps you.
It doesn't help me, but I'm not the one down there.
It was fair. Cruel and fair aren't opposites.
It is. I'll be carrying it a long time.
You don't have to carry it with me. That's all.
Knowing what I know now? No.
Knowing what I knew then? Yes. Every time.
That's the whole problem with being a historian.
They've asked me to ask you to come up. For the file.
I told them it's quarantine and you'd say no anyway.
Would you? If the Doctor cleared it?

options.text: No. Somebody has to stay down here.
Ask me when he's cleared it.

lines.text: Then I hope he's quick. I really do.
Until then the beacons are yours. Shepard out.
Now you know why I stayed. Shepard out.
Fair. I'll ask. He'll say not yet. Shepard out.
